paper.title: Toward New Candidates for Hydrogen Storage: High-Surface-Area Carbon Aerogels

defaults.verified_by: Agent B (sonnet, independent re-extraction of Table 1 + text): 9 BET/wt% pairs, 0 numeric disputes (Ni 970/2.3 at 800 C and 1100/2.0 at 1050 C not transposed). Pressure confirmed: only the 3200 m2/g ACA has an explicit 30 bar; the other 8 are genuine surface-excess saturation values with pressure_unstated (the '~30 bar'/'~35 bar' statements are collective/literature, not per-sample). uptake_type=excess ('surface excess') confirmed. synthesis_method split confirmed: undoped ACAs CO2-activated (physical_activation), Ni/Co pyrolyzed only (pyrolysis); Co surface_area_method=not_reported confirmed. The 330 m2/g non-carbonized organic aerogel correctly excluded. material_class=composite for Ni/Co endorsed (discrete metal nanoparticles = two-phase, not lattice doping). No changes.

notes.type: uptake_type=excess (exact-word rule): the paper reports 'hydrogen surface excess sorption' / 'H2 surface excess saturation value' throughout (abstract, Figs 1-2, Table 1)
notes.sat: the recorded value is the saturation maximum of the surface-excess isotherm at 77 K (Table 1 'H2 (wt%)'); it is the peak of the excess trace, not a fixed-pressure reading
notes.p3200: only the 3200 m2/g ACA has an explicit pressure: '5.3 wt% at 30 bar' (abstract, text); recorded at 30 bar
notes.punstated: for every sample except the 3200 m2/g ACA the per-sample saturation pressure is not stated: the text gives only a general '~30 bar for higher surface area materials' and the isotherms span 0-40 bar; imputing a per-sample pressure would fabricate a condition, so pressure_unstated=True (HYC-0011/0015 precedent)
notes.method: H2 adsorption/desorption excess sorption by a volumetric Sieverts apparatus; the paper states no H2 purity, no sample mass and describes no explicit void-volume/buoyancy correction, so no calibration point
notes.aca: undoped activated carbon aerogel: sol-gel polymerization of resorcinol-formaldehyde, supercritically dried, pyrolyzed, then CO2-activated at 950 C; class=carbon_aerogel, synthesis_method=physical_activation (CO2 activation); the sample is labelled by its BET surface area
notes.metal: Ni-/Co-modified carbon aerogels are metal-bearing -> class 'composite' with metal_element (HYC-0027/29/39/40 convention); these are pyrolyzed but NOT CO2-activated ('The undoped CAs were then activated with CO2'), so synthesis_method=pyrolysis; metal nanoparticles homogeneously distributed in the CA network; metal loading not quantified
notes.cosa: Co-modified CA: the paper reports no BET surface area for the Co samples (areas are given only for the undoped ACAs and the two Ni samples), so surface_area_method=not_reported
notes.org: the 330 m2/g organic aerogel (0.8 wt% at 20 bar) is explicitly 'not carbonized' / 'prior to carbonization' -- it is not a carbon material and is excluded
notes.chahine: 77 K saturation excess; ACA 3200 at 30 bar gives 5.3 wt% ~ 3200/500=6.4 Chahine estimate, physically consistent (the paper's own point is the linear ~1 wt% per 500 m2/g law)
